question: Should a 5-person startup use cloud LLM APIs or self-host an open-source model?

plan.main_question: Should a 5-person startup use cloud LLM APIs or self-host an open-source model?
plan.decision_context: A 5-person startup is evaluating whether to rely on managed cloud LLM APIs (like OpenAI or Anthropic) or self-host open-source models (like Llama 3) to minimize costs and operational overhead.

subquestions.question: What are the comparative monthly costs of cloud LLM APIs versus self-hosting open-source models on cloud GPUs for a small startup volume?

decision.rationale: All three specialists are utilized to cover costs, technical implementation, performance, and compliance aspects for a startup infrastructure decision, using standard depth for a balanced evaluation.

summaries.sq1: Cloud LLM APIs are more cost-effective for small startup volumes below a break-even threshold of 1 to 3 billion tokens per month [ev2, ev3, ev6]. Self-hosting on a single rented inference GPU costs $1.50 to $4.00 per hour ($1,100 to $2,900 monthly for 24/7 operation) [ev1], while larger 70B models require multiple GPUs [ev4]. Furthermore, engineering labor for self-hosting requires 0.25 to 0.5 of a full-time engineer [ev7].

summaries.sq2: Self-hosting open-source LLMs requires significant engineering and operational effort, making it a heavy burden for a 5-person startup [ev13]. Evidence indicates that routine tasks like driver updates can break serving containers and cause extended downtime when there is no dedicated on-call rotation [ev11]. Handling memory management and out-of-memory crashes under load from long prompts requires weeks of tuning batch sizes [ev12]. While stable operation is possible when an organization has a dedicated infrastructure engineer [ev14], for small teams without one, self-hosting requires constant babysitting [ev13]. Open issues: Specific quantitative estimates of DevOps hours from the academic report could not be fully extracted due to source constraints, relying instead on real-world team experiences.
summaries.sq3: Dedicated GPU deployments for self-hosted models achieve faster and more consistent median time-to-first-token latency (approximately 120 milliseconds for short prompts) compared to shared commercial APIs (ranging from 250 to 600 milliseconds) [ev15]. At the 99th percentile, shared APIs can experience latency of several seconds during peak traffic hours, whereas dedicated GPUs maintain sub-second latency until reaching hardware capacity [ev16]. However, shared APIs enforce rate limits that require retry logic [ev17], and self-hosted dedicated GPUs suffer sharp latency increases when concurrent requests exceed capacity, necessitating additional GPU provisioning [ev18].

summaries.sq4: Self-hosting models allows organizations to implement their own access controls and audit logs for prompts involving sensitive data [ev9]. However, self-hosting requires organizations to manage their own security responsibilities—such as verifying model weights and patching infrastructure—which would otherwise be handled by a third-party provider [ev8], and it does not inherently protect against prompt injection attacks [ev10]. Furthermore, regulatory compliance obligations (such as for financial institutions) remain regardless of deployment method, requiring in-house deployments to demonstrate proper access controls, audit logging, model change management, and incident response [ev19, ev20]. Open issues: Specific details on HIPAA or SOC2 framework advantages for self-hosted vs cloud API models were not directly covered by the saved sources.

agreements: Self-hosting and dedicated inference setups require organizations to take on maintenance, operational burdens, and specific security responsibilities such as access control and audit logging [ev7, ev8, ev9, ev13, ev20]
Hosted APIs are generally more cost-effective or lower TCO for low-volume users or small teams compared to self-hosting [ev1, ev2, ev3, ev6]

report.title: Cloud LLM APIs versus Self-Hosting Open-Source Models for a 5-Person Startup
report.executive_summary: A 5-person startup should rely on managed cloud LLM APIs rather than self-hosting open-source models. Self-hosting introduces significant operational overhead and engineering labor, requiring 0.25 to 0.5 of a full-time engineer, which is prohibitive for a small team. Furthermore, cloud APIs provide a lower total cost of ownership at volumes below the 1 to 3 billion token break-even threshold. This recommendation depends on the startup operating below high-volume thresholds where dedicated infrastructure becomes financially justified.

findings.statement: Renting a single inference-class GPU on-demand costs $1,100 to $2,900 per month for 24/7 operation, making self-hosting more expensive than cloud APIs below a volume threshold of 1 to 3 billion tokens per month.
Hosted APIs offer lower total cost of ownership for small teams with low request volumes compared to self-hosting.
Keeping a self-hosted model reliable in production requires 0.25 to 0.5 of a full-time engineer for ongoing maintenance, patching, and monitoring.
Small teams running self-hosted models face operational risks such as out-of-memory crashes under load, driver updates breaking serving containers, and the need for constant monitoring.

Dedicated GPU deployments achieve faster time-to-first-token for short prompts (around 120 milliseconds) compared to shared APIs (250 to 600 milliseconds), though they risk sharp latency increases or errors when capacity limits are exceeded.
Self-hosting requires organizations to manage their own security responsibilities, such as verifying model weights against checksums and implementing access controls and audit logs.
At volumes below the break-even threshold, the GPU sits idle much of the time and self-hosting results in a higher effective cost per token than using an API.

limitations: Cost analyses for self-hosting often exclude the hidden burden of engineering labor and incident response.
Evidence for operational failures and maintenance burden largely stems from anecdotal forum posts rather than rigorous quantitative studies.
report.recommendation: Use managed cloud LLM APIs for the startup's current operations to avoid high engineering overhead and infrastructure maintenance. Revisit self-hosting and evaluate dedicated GPU deployment only if monthly token volumes exceed 1 billion or strict regulatory compliance demands in-house data control.
